4 أَعَاهُوا and أَعْوَهُوا , (S, Msb, K,) the latter mentioned by El-Umawee, (S,) and ↓ عِوّهوا . (IAar, K,) They had their cattle, (S, Msb, K,) or their seed-produce, (K,) or their fruits, (TA,) smitten with what is termed عَاهَة [i. e. a bane, such as a disease, pest, or murrain, or a blight, blast, taint, canker, or the like]. (S, Msb, K, TA.) ―
-b2- See also 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
